summary:
"Let’s Find It" (*Juguemos a encontrar*) is a project consisting of three main components. It begins with a website featuring thirteen pieces of abandoned equipment located on various celestial bodies, each accompanied by a narrative tailored for children aged 7 to 12. For those who wish to delve deeper, the site provides details on the equipment’s discoveries, the reasons it ceased to function, and other intriguing facts. Additionally, there is a trivia-style game that allows children to reinforce what they have learned in an engaging and educational way. Finally, the project includes a downloadable board game, which can serve as a teaching resource for primary school educators.
We chose to approach this challenge from an educational perspective, focusing on children’s learning, as the study of the universe is a fundamental pillar of the social sciences curriculum in primary education.
details: The "Let’s Play and Discover" ("Juguemos a Encontrar") initiative is an educational model designed for learning about the universe within the field of Social Sciences. It is built upon three cornerstones, following an "EJE" learning framework (Listen, Play, and Evaluate). The website—a narrative collection detailing 13 pieces of equipment left behind in space (the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge)—provides the visual and conceptual tools for introducing the subject matter ("Listen"). A board game serves as the project’s core interactive element, available for download and play ("Play"). Finally, a digital trivia game completes the cycle by testing and assessing the concepts covered ("Evaluate"). This model fosters knowledge acquisition among students; when implemented, it promises to make classroom sessions more dynamic, encouraging active learning and sparking genuine interest in the topics presented. The project was developed using JavaScript, CSS, and HTML, with the design created via the Canva platform. It stands out for its creative, alternative approach to the subject matter—adopting a playful perspective—driven by the guiding question: "How can we share our solution in an engaging and fun way?"
